output.answer_markdown: Fox described exposure to two types of market risk: changes in interest rates and stock prices [1]. It explained that fixed-rate and variable-rate debt are affected differently by interest rate changes. A change in the rate or yield on fixed-rate debt affects only that debt's fair market value. A change in the rate on variable-rate debt affects interest expense and the cash needed to service the debt [2]. Its financing arrangements and facilities included $7.25 billion of outstanding fixed-rate debt, before adjustments for unamortized discount and debt issuance costs [3]. As of June 30, 2022, no variable-rate debt was outstanding [4], and there were no borrowings under the Revolving Credit Agreement [5].
